OWNED FILES: storygame/runtime/fixed_refusal.py, storygame/runtime/capture.py (edit); tests/test_fixed_refusal.py (edit). Edit nothing else.

DEFECT (found by running the real scene, not by the unit tests): `refuse_fixed_move` only considers a fixed item when `world.area(item_id) == world.area(protagonist)`. In real play in scene 1A the protagonist's area is 'Michelle's house' while the workstation, back door and drawer are in the 'kitchen' sub-area and the truck seats are 'outside the house', so the equality is false and the step NEVER asks the question. The existing tests passed because they placed the player in the same area by hand.

FIX: give `refuse_fixed_move` an optional keyword `in_scope: Callable[[str], bool] | None = None`. When given, a fixed item is a candidate when `in_scope(item_id)` is true (still also fixed, visible, not an area). When None, keep today's same-area test so existing behaviour and tests do not change. In capture.py `WorldCapture.before_turn` pass `in_scope=lambda item_id: self.provider._name_in_scene_scope(world, world.name(item_id))` (the engine's existing definition of scene scope in storygame/runtime/item_facts.py: scene items and participants plus anything at or below the scene's area or the protagonist's area). Do not change `_name_in_scene_scope`.

TESTS (edit tests/test_fixed_refusal.py, hermetic): add tests that start from the REAL scene-1A state, not a hand-placed one: build the state as `st = RuntimeState.bootstrap(package); st.current_scene_id = '1A'; apply_scene_placements(package, st.facts, '1A')`, then `provider = build_capture_provider(st)` and `provider._ensure_scene_seeded()`; `world = provider._world()`. First assert as a precondition that the protagonist's area differs from the workstation's area (this documents the defect). Cases: (a) without in_scope the workstation is NOT a candidate in this state (documents the old limit); (b) with in_scope=lambda i: provider._name_in_scene_scope(world, world.name(i)) the command 'Carry the workstation to the truck.' with a True stub gives the exact sentence 'Kristin tried to move the workstation. It is fixed in place and did not move.'; (c) the same for 'Detach the driver's seat from the truck.' (driver's seat) and 'Extract the drawer from the workstation.' (the drawer, whose parent is the workstation); (d) a WorldCapture(provider, ask, fixed_refusal=True) integration in this real state: patch `CloudflareTurnProvider._request` with unittest.mock so prepare_turn's match call returns {'refers': ['workstation'], 'same_as': {}}; the ask stub answers True for the relocates_thing key; assert `before_turn('Carry the workstation to the truck.')['steps'][0]` is the sentence, `provider.prior_steps` starts with it, and after `provider.assemble_turn_prompt(command)` the rendered user prompt (`pr.get('user') or provider._section_user_prompt(pr['context'])`) contains 'Just before this: Kristin tried to move the workstation.'; and that none of the stand/board/take/seat question keys were asked; (e) with the ask stub answering False for 'Examine the workstation.' no 'Just before this' line appears. Keep all existing assertions. If a case cannot be built as described, adapt to the nearest real behaviour and say so in notes; never weaken (d).

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the cwd. Tests need CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example/t and CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN=x set in the environment for build_capture_provider to construct (no network call is made when _request is patched): PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example/t CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN=x /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_fixed_refusal.py tests/test_bench_runtime_mode.py tests/test_runtime_capture.py tests/test_refusal_modes.py tests/test_web_demo.py. Check how tests/test_runtime_capture.py handles those environment variables and follow its pattern (monkeypatch.setenv) so the new tests do not depend on the shell. Also `-k "bench or capture or taking or seating or jev or item_facts"` over tests/. Ruff: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix and -m ruff format on every file you changed. Reply with the files changed.
